item.title: Trump Threatens to Withdraw Blanche as Attorney General, Dealing Blow to Nomination
item.description: President Trump’s threat followed a day of fruitless negotiations with two Republican holdouts, Senators John Cornyn and Thom Tillis.
item.dc:creator: Glenn Thrush, Michael Gold and Carl Hulse
item.media:description: The two senators object to a deal negotiated by Todd Blanche and President Trump’s personal lawyers to resolve a lawsuit the president had filed against the I.R.S.

item.title: Why Todd Blanche’s Attorney General Confirmation Is Stalled
item.description: The decision by the acting attorney general, Todd Blanche, to grant President Trump protection from I.R.S. audits has become the central issue in his confirmation process.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Duehren
item.media:credit: Haiyun Jiang for The New York Times
item.media:description: President Trump’s extraordinary protection from the I.R.S. is expected to be a central issue in the confirmation hearing on Wednesday.

item.title: Big Tech’s A.I. Spending Keeps Rising. So Do the Jitters.
item.description: Amazon joined a procession of tech giants that ramped up their spending on artificial intelligence, as its capital expenditures soared 69 percent. Concerns over the industry’s spending are mounting.
item.dc:creator: Karen Weise
item.media:credit: Christie Hemm Klok for The New York Times
item.media:description: Meta’s Eagle Mountain Data Center in Utah. Meta, Amazon, Google and Microsoft are expected to spend $1.5 trillion building data centers through next year.

item.title: Apple’s Profit Increases 27 Percent, Topping Wall Street Expectations
item.description: The company recently raised prices on a number of products because of component supply shortages caused by the artificial intelligence boom.
item.dc:creator: Kalley Huang
item.media:description: Apple regained its spot as the world’s most valuable publicly traded company earlier this week.

item.title: A.I. Hedge Fund Situational Awareness Rescued by Rival Citadel
item.description: The once-high-flying firm Situational Awareness, whose founder is 24, has been bailed out by Kenneth Griffin’s Citadel, according to three people briefed on the transaction.
item.dc:creator: Rob Copeland
item.media:credit: Nicholas Albrecht for The New York Times
item.media:description: Situational Awareness was named after a 2024 essay by its founder, Leopold Aschenbrenner, 24, that predicted research labs would develop a superintelligent form of A.I. by 2027.

item.title: Elon Musk Plans at Least $100 Million in Midterm Spending to Help Republicans
item.description: Elon Musk, a year after a huge blowup with President Trump and the Republican Party, is said to be planning to spend in at least eight states to help them in November.
item.dc:creator: Theodore Schleifer
item.media:credit: Jim Vondruska for The New York Times
item.media:description: Elon Musk was the biggest donor in the 2024 presidential election, when he spent hundreds of millions.

item.title: Former Lt. Gov. Mandela Barnes Exits Race for Wisconsin Governor
item.description: With a democratic socialist, Francesca Hong, leading in polls, former Lt. Gov. Mandela Barnes said he was ending his campaign in the closely divided state.
item.dc:creator: Mitch Smith
item.media:credit: Jenn Ackerman for The New York Times
item.media:description: Mandela Barnes, a former lieutenant governor of Wisconsin, in Madison in June.

item.title: How Haley Stevens’s Accent Became a Flashpoint in Michigan’s Senate Race
item.description: How the politics of raised a’s and disappearing g’s briefly came to dominate the Michigan Senate race.
item.dc:creator: Matt Flegenheimer
item.media:description: “I am your voice,” said Representative Haley Stevens, a four-term congresswoman who is running for Senate in Michigan, after her accent was mocked online.

item.title: Spain Mobilizes Military as Thousands of Migrants Cross Into Ceuta
item.description: The arrivals in Ceuta, a six-mile-long peninsula on Morocco’s northern coast that Spain has governed for centuries, have fueled political tensions.
item.dc:creator: Jason Horowitz
item.media:description: Migrants crossing from Morocco into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta on Thursday.

item.title: Who Put Candy on a Diet?
item.description: “Healthy” confections, whether marketed as “better-for-you” or “functional,” have overwhelmed grocery and convenience stores, and even found their way into gyms and supplement shops.
item.dc:creator: Ella Quittner
item.media:credit: Scott Semler for The New York Times. Prop stylist: Maggie DiMarco.

item.title: Trump’s Tariff Exemptions Include Diamonds, Oil and Gas, Copper and Other Items
item.description: A new round of tariff carve-outs has raised familiar questions about who should receive the lucrative exceptions, and why.
item.dc:creator: Ana Swanson and Jeanna Smialek
item.category: Office of the United States Trade Representative
item.media:description: A diamond group in Antwerp, Belgium, designed an 18-karat gold ring encrusted with 321 diamonds and dozens of sapphires, emeralds and rubies in honor of America’s 250th anniversary.

item.title: U.S. GDP Growth Slowed in Second Quarter of 2026
item.description: Gross domestic product grew at a slower rate in the second quarter and persistent price pressures are unsettling financial markets.
item.dc:creator: Talmon Joseph Smith

item.title: Why Democrats Won’t Stop Forcing Votes On Trump’s Iran War Powers
item.description: Even after winning approval of a measure calling on President Trump to end the war, they continue to call votes to force Republicans to answer for it.
item.dc:creator: Robert Jimison
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:description: Senator Kirsten Gillibrand, Democrat of New York, put forward this week the latest measure to rein in the president’s war powers.

item.title: Attack on Egyptian Port Shows Suez Canal’s Vulnerability
item.description: The port where the Wednesday strike occurred is near the Suez Canal, through which a significant amount of the world’s shipping moves.
item.dc:creator: Lynsey Chutel
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:description: Ships in the Suez Canal last year. About 10 percent of seaborne trade goes through the waterway, according to the Suez Canal Authority.

item.title: U.S. Sees Iran as Likely Behind Cyberattack on Minnesota Water Systems
item.description: Investigators cautioned that the assessment was preliminary. There were no indications that any water supply had been rendered unsafe to drink.
item.dc:creator: Dustin Volz and Ernesto Londoño
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:credit: Jenn Ackerman for The New York Times
item.media:description: Dozens of municipal water systems in Minnesota were the targets of a cyberattack this week.

item.title: A Bay Area Pastor Made an A.I. Twin to Talk About God at Any Time
item.description: To meet the growing needs of his congregation, Justin Lester created an A.I. duplicate of himself. Every day he sees more people using it.
item.dc:creator: Eli Saslow and Erin Schaff

item.title: DOJ Seeks to Use Court to Deport Mother of Convicted ISIS Supporter
item.description: The case is a test of the Alien Terrorist Removal Court, where much of the evidence is presented in secret and defendants cannot challenge how it was collected.
item.dc:creator: Alan Feuer and Adam Sella
item.category: Islamic State in Iraq and Syria (ISIS)
item.media:description: The Justice Department headquarters in Washington last month.

item.title: Ebola Outbreak Is Now the Second-Deadliest Ever, and in Record Time
item.description: The disease has killed more than 1,500 people in the Democratic Republic of Congo in just over two months, causing deaths faster than officials have ever recorded.
item.dc:creator: Zane Irwin and Stephanie Nolen
item.category: Africa Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
item.media:credit: Finbarr O'Reilly for The New York Times
item.media:description: Health workers at an Ebola treatment center in the Democratic Republic of Congo, in June.

item.title: Colin Gray, Father of Teenage Shooter in Georgia, Sentenced to 15 Years in Prison
item.description: Prosecutors argued that Colin Gray bore responsibility for the 2024 shooting because he had given his son a gun and failed to act as the teen’s mental health deteriorated.
item.dc:creator: Rick Rojas and Johnny Kauffman
item.media:description: Colin Gray was convicted in March of murder and other offenses in connection with the deadly shooting carried out by his son, Colt Gray, at Apalachee High School.

item.title: After Claiming ‘Bias’ at Smithsonian, Trump Officials Stage Patriotic Exhibition
item.description: Trump officials have promised to “make visual arts great,” with a museum exhibition that includes artwork by several people with personal connections to the planners.
item.dc:creator: Zachary Small
item.media:credit: Caroline Gutman for The New York Times
item.media:description: The fashion designer Kate Wasserbach Moore produced a silk dress, “America250 Gown,” for the exhibition “Passport to Patriotism” at the Art Museum of the Americas. Erin Scavino, one of the organizers, met the designer while shopping for her own wedding dress.

item.title: For Museum Boss Who Became a Trump Target, It’s Déjà Vu All Over Again
item.description: Kim Sajet left as director of the National Portrait Gallery when she found herself in the White House cross hairs. Now she’s watching another Smithsonian chief go through it.
item.dc:creator: Robin Pogrebin
item.media:credit: Taylor Glascock for The New York Times
item.media:description: Last year, Kim Sajet of the National Portrait Gallery was targeted by President Trump, who described her as “highly partisan.” “I could see that it was going to become a real witch hunt,” she said of resigning.

item.title: ‘This Is Very Strange’: Ancient Smallpox May Have Been Less Deadly
item.description: Scientists have found smallpox viruses in the remains of people in Chile from around 500 years ago, revealing how the virus may have evolved into a global killer.
item.dc:creator: Carl Zimmer
